B2a-08-rhizopus-mould-structure

Rhizopus growing on a slice of bread. Left: a slice of bread with patches of white fluffy mould and black dots. Right: an enlarged drawing of the mould: horizontal stolons arching over the bread surface; at each point where a stolon touches the bread, a cluster of branched rhizoids going down into the bread and a group of upright sporangiophores going up, each ending in a round black sporangium full of spores; one sporangium bursting to release spores. Show small arrows from the rhizoid tips into the bread labelled as enzymes, and arrows back into the rhizoids labelled as soluble food absorbed.
B2a-01-autotrophic-versus-heterotrophic-nutrition

Two-panel comparison diagram of the two modes of nutrition. Left panel, "autotrophic": a green maize plant in sunlight, with arrows showing CO₂ entering a leaf from the air, water and mineral salts entering the roots from the soil, and oxygen leaving the leaf; a sun in the corner; a small glucose molecule symbol inside the leaf. Right panel, "heterotrophic": a goat eating grass, a mushroom growing on a fallen log, and a tapeworm inside a section of intestine, with arrows showing ready-made food entering each organism.
B2a-04-human-digestive-system

The human digestive system shown as a simple front view inside an outline of the head and torso: mouth with teeth and tongue, salivary glands, oesophagus, J-shaped stomach, liver with gall bladder, pancreas, duodenum, coiled ileum, large intestine (colon) framing it, small caecum with appendix in the lower right of the body, rectum and anus. Soft natural colours.
B2a-05-ascaris-morphology-infection

Two panels. Left: an adult male and female Ascaris lumbricoides roundworm side by side, long, cylindrical and pinkish-white, the female larger with a straight tail, the male smaller with a curled tail; an enlarged front-end view showing the mouth with three lips. Right: a cut-open section of the human small intestine with several roundworms lying in the cavity among food.
B2a-06-tapeworm-structure-scolex

Two panels. Left: a whole tapeworm (Taenia), drawn as a long ribbon looping across the panel: a tiny scolex, a thin neck, small immature proglottids near the neck becoming larger and square further back, and long mature proglottids at the end, one breaking off. Right: an enlarged scolex showing a ring of hooks (rostellum) at the top and four round suckers, attached to the villi of the intestine wall. Pale cream worm on a light pink gut background.
B2a-07-mistletoe-parasitism

Two parts. Main picture: a branch of an orange tree with a bushy Loranthus (African mistletoe) plant growing out of it, with thick green leathery leaves and clusters of red-orange tubular flowers, and a sunbird feeding at a flower. Inset: a longitudinal section through the junction of mistletoe and host branch, showing the host's bark, phloem and xylem, and the mistletoe's haustorium pushing through the bark and joining the host xylem, with small blue arrows showing water and mineral salts passing from the host into the mistletoe.
B2a-09-mushroom-anatomy-mycelium

A mushroom growing from rotting leaves and a fallen log, with the soil cut away to show the underground mycelium. Show a mushroom with a cap, gills underneath (one half of the cap cut to show the gills), a stalk with a ring, a cup at the base, and a large network of fine white hyphae spreading through dead leaves and wood below. A small inset shows hyphal tips with arrows: enzymes going out, soluble food coming in.
B2a-10-sundew-insect-trap-mechanism

A sundew (Drosera) plant and an enlarged leaf. Left: a small rosette plant with spoon-shaped leaves covered in red hair-like tentacles, each with a glistening drop at its tip, on wet ground. Right: two stages of a single leaf: (1) a small fly stuck on the drops of the tentacles, with the tentacles straight; (2) the tentacles bent over and pressing the fly to the leaf centre. A small inset of one tentacle showing the stalk and the gland with its sticky drop.
B2a-03-ruminant-stomach

The four-chambered stomach of a sheep (ruminant), shown as a simplified cut-open diagram with arrows tracing the path of food. Oesophagus entering at the top; a very large rumen with grass and small microbe symbols inside; the smaller reticulum next to it with a honeycomb-patterned lining; a curved arrow going back up the oesophagus to the mouth labelled as cud being regurgitated and re-chewed; the omasum with many leaf-like folds; the long tube-like abomasum leading to the small intestine. Numbered arrows 1 to 5 showing the order: oesophagus → rumen → reticulum → mouth (re-chewing) → omasum → abomasum → small intestine. Soft colours: rumen green-brown, reticulum light brown, omasum tan, abomasum pink.
B2a-11-bladderwort-trap-mechanism

A bladderwort (Utricularia) and a cut-open bladder. Left: a floating plant in a pond with fine, thread-like branched underwater leaves carrying many tiny bladders, and small yellow two-lipped flowers held above the water on a stalk. Right: an enlarged longitudinal section of one bladder in two stages: (1) set, with the walls pulled slightly inwards, the door closed and a water flea approaching the trigger hairs; (2) sprung, with the door swung open inwards, arrows showing water and the water flea being sucked in.
B2a-02-classification-nutrition-flowchart

Flow chart of the modes and types of nutrition. Top box "Nutrition" splitting into two boxes "Autotrophic" and "Heterotrophic". Under Autotrophic: "Photosynthetic (green plants, algae)" and "Chemosynthetic (nitrifying bacteria)". Under Heterotrophic: "Holozoic (sheep, man)", "Parasitic (roundworm, tapeworm, Loranthus)", "Saprophytic (Rhizopus, mushroom)", "Symbiotic (Rhizobium and legumes, lichens)". A side box joined to both main branches by dotted lines: "Carnivorous plants (sundew, bladderwort): photosynthesise and digest insects". Each lower box has a small simple icon of the example. Labels are the box texts given. Soft pastel colours: green for autotrophic, orange for heterotrophic.
